title: 3rd Point: The Necessity of Prophethood from Beauty and Art in the Universe

questions.question: What central claim is made at the beginning of the passage about beauty in the universe and the mission of Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him?
questions.answer: The passage says that the beauty and artistry seen throughout creation point decisively to his messengership.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the beauty found in created things show about their Maker?
questions.answer: It shows that the Maker has a strong will to make things beautiful and a powerful desire to adorn them.

questions.question: What deeper quality of the Maker is inferred from this will to beautify and adorn?
questions.answer: It points to a lofty love and sacred inclination toward the perfections displayed in His creation.

questions.question: Toward which created being is this divine love said to be directed most strongly?
questions.answer: It is said to be directed most strongly toward the human being.

questions.question: Why is the human being given that special place in the argument?
questions.answer: Because the human being is presented as the conscious and most comprehensive fruit of creation.

questions.question: What qualities should the most distinguished human possess according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should have the widest awareness and deepest understanding, and he should devote these fully to worship, gratitude, and appreciating divine artistry.

questions.question: How is the highest human described in relation to the Maker?
questions.answer: He is described as one who meets with and receives address from the Maker.

questions.question: What are the two “spheres” mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: One is the realm of divine rule and artistic display, and the other is the realm of worship, reflection, admiration, gratitude, and faith.

questions.question: How is the first sphere characterized?
questions.answer: It is described as majestic, orderly, and filled with finely crafted beauty.

questions.question: How is the second sphere characterized?
questions.answer: It is described as radiant and broad, expressing worship, thought, wonder, thankfulness, and belief.

questions.question: What relationship does the second sphere have to the first?
questions.answer: It serves the first with all its strength and acts on its behalf.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the connection between these two spheres?
questions.answer: The leader of the second sphere must be very closely connected to the Maker and deeply loved and accepted by Him.

questions.question: What reasoning is used to argue that the Maker would not ignore such a servant?
questions.answer: Since the Maker cares even for small human tastes, it would be unreasonable to think He would neglect His finest creature who responds with intense worship and praise.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the effect of this servant’s worship and gratitude?
questions.answer: His praise and thanks are described as so powerful that they echo through creation.

questions.question: What two actions of the Maker toward this servant are presented as necessary rather than optional?
questions.answer: Speaking to him and appointing him as Messenger are presented as necessary.

questions.question: What final religious conclusion closes the passage?
questions.answer: The passage ends by affirming Islam as the true religion before Allah and Muhammad, peace be upon him, as Allah’s Messenger.

questions.question: Which observable feature of the universe is used as evidence in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage uses the visible beauty and artistry of the universe as evidence.

questions.question: What does that observed beauty make necessary, according to the argument?
questions.answer: It makes the messengership of Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, necessary.

questions.question: How certain is this conclusion said to be?
questions.answer: It is said to be as certain as direct witnessing.

questions.question: What do elegant forms and artistic creation reveal about the Creator’s intention?
questions.answer: They reveal an intention to produce beauty and adornment.

questions.question: After establishing divine intention, what emotional or relational attribute is then inferred?
questions.answer: A holy love for the perfection found in His own art is inferred.

questions.question: Why does the passage move from creation in general to the human being in particular?
questions.answer: Because the argument says the divine appreciation of beauty would be focused most on the human being, who is the most aware and complete creature.

questions.question: What image is used to explain the human being’s place in creation?
questions.answer: The human being is compared to the fruit of a tree.

questions.question: In that image, why is the fruit important?
questions.answer: The fruit is important because it gathers the meanings of the tree and stands at its furthest and most complete point.

questions.question: Among human beings, what kind of person is singled out as most fitting for special closeness to the Maker?
questions.answer: The person with the broadest perception and most universal awareness is singled out.

questions.question: What should this person do with those gifts of awareness and understanding?
questions.answer: He should spend them in worship, appreciating divine artistry, and thanking Allah for His blessings.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by speaking of two signboards or displays?
questions.answer: It means there are two great manifestations: one showing divine artistry and rule, and the other showing worship and understanding in response.

questions.question: What does the second display contain?
questions.answer: It contains worship, reflection, admiration, gratitude, and faith.

questions.question: Why is the leader of the second sphere so important in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Because he represents the fullest human response to the divine artistry shown in the first sphere.

questions.question: What example is used to show that the Maker is attentive and generous even in small matters?
questions.answer: The passage points to the way human tastes of the mouth are taken into account.

questions.question: Based on that example, what would be unreasonable to believe?
questions.answer: It would be unreasonable to believe that the Maker would ignore the most beautiful servant who turns to Him with deep praise and gratitude.

questions.question: What is said to be impossible concerning that servant?
questions.answer: It is said to be impossible that the Maker would neither speak to him nor appoint him as Messenger.

questions.question: How do the final Qur’anic statements support the argument just made?
questions.answer: They sum it up by affirming Islam as the religion accepted by Allah and Muhammad, peace be upon him, as His Messenger.

questions.question: What is the main line of reasoning in the passage?
questions.answer: It argues from the beauty in creation to the Creator’s love of perfection, then to the need for a supreme human responder, and finally to the messengership of Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat beauty in the universe as more than decoration?
questions.answer: Because it is presented as a sign of divine purpose, will, and love.

questions.question: What does the presence of refined artistry suggest about the Creator’s attributes?
questions.answer: It suggests intentional beauty-making and a powerful desire to embellish creation.

questions.question: How does the passage connect artistic intention to love?
questions.answer: It says that the urge to produce such perfection indicates a deep love for the excellences shown in that art.

questions.question: Why would this love be especially directed toward human beings?
questions.answer: Because humans are described as the most conscious, enlightened, and complete creatures.

questions.question: What role does consciousness play in the argument?
questions.answer: Consciousness makes the human being able to recognize, reflect on, and respond to divine beauty.

questions.question: What kind of human response is presented as the highest one?
questions.answer: Wholehearted worship, thoughtful reflection, admiration, gratitude, and faith are presented as the highest response.

questions.question: Which human being is implied to embody that response in the fullest way?
questions.answer: Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, is implied to embody it in the fullest way.

questions.question: What is the purpose of introducing the two spheres?
questions.answer: The two spheres show the harmony between divine action and human worshipful response.

questions.question: How does the second sphere relate to the divine purposes shown in the first sphere?
questions.answer: It supports and serves those purposes by recognizing, praising, and thanking the Maker.

questions.question: Who stands at the center of the second sphere?
questions.answer: Its leader stands at the center, meaning the foremost servant who responds most perfectly.

questions.question: What does his leadership indicate about his standing with Allah?
questions.answer: It indicates special nearness, acceptance, and belovedness.

questions.question: How does the passage use a question-and-answer style to strengthen its claim?
questions.answer: It asks whether such a generous and beauty-loving Maker could ignore His finest worshipper, then answers that this cannot be so.

questions.question: What is the significance of mentioning the Throne, earth, land, and sea?
questions.answer: These images show the vast reach and powerful effect of that servant’s worship and praise.

questions.question: What does the argument imply about revelation?
questions.answer: It implies that revelation is fitting and necessary for the servant who most perfectly responds to Allah and represents that response to others.

questions.question: Besides speaking to him, what else would the Maker want according to the passage?
questions.answer: The Maker would want that servant’s praiseworthy way to be conveyed to other people.

questions.question: What final doctrinal truths are explicitly affirmed at the end?
questions.answer: That Islam is the religion before Allah and that Muhammad, peace be upon him, is the Messenger of Allah.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can be learned from the beauty of created things?
questions.answer: One can learn that the Creator intentionally makes things beautiful and adorned.

questions.question: Why is intention important in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Because it shows creation is not random but reflects purposeful divine action.

questions.question: What does purposeful beauty further indicate about the Creator’s inner relation to His art?
questions.answer: It indicates a sacred love for the excellences displayed in that art.

questions.question: Why does the argument not stop at nature itself?
questions.answer: Because it moves from divine artistry to the need for a conscious creature who can understand and answer it.

questions.question: Which creature is identified as best suited for that response?
questions.answer: The human being is identified as best suited for it.

questions.question: What metaphor explains the human being’s relation to the whole universe?
questions.answer: The human being is described as the fruit of the tree of creation.

questions.question: What does that metaphor suggest about human responsibility?
questions.answer: It suggests that human beings gather the meanings of creation and should respond to Allah knowingly and gratefully.

questions.question: What distinguishes the greatest human from other people in the passage?
questions.answer: He has the broadest awareness and uses it completely for worship and thankfulness.

questions.question: What kind of encounter with the Maker is mentioned for this greatest human?
questions.answer: He is described as one who is addressed by the Maker.

questions.question: What are the two broad realities displayed before us in the passage?
questions.answer: One is the display of divine lordship and art, and the other is the display of worshipful human response.

questions.question: Why is the second reality said to act in the name of the first?
questions.answer: Because it answers the first by recognizing its meaning and giving it conscious praise and thanks.

questions.question: What does this say about the one who leads the second reality?
questions.answer: It shows that he is uniquely connected to the divine purpose manifested in creation.

questions.question: How does the passage appeal to reason when discussing the Maker’s treatment of that leader?
questions.answer: It argues that a Creator so attentive and generous would surely not leave His greatest praising servant without communication and mission.

questions.question: What small human experience is mentioned to illustrate divine generosity?
questions.answer: Human taste and enjoyment in eating are mentioned.

questions.question: What larger conclusion is drawn from that small example?
questions.answer: If such minor needs are cared for, then the highest spiritual servant would all the more be honored with revelation and messengership.

questions.question: Why is it said that the Maker would want this servant’s way to spread to others?
questions.answer: Because his conduct is worthy of being followed and serves the divine purposes reflected in creation.

questions.question: How do the closing declarations function in relation to the whole passage?
questions.answer: They present the final belief statement that matches the reasoning: Islam is the true religion before Allah, and Muhammad, peace be upon him, is His Messenger.

questions.question: What visible evidence does the passage begin with?
questions.answer: It begins with the visible beauty and craftsmanship present in the universe.

questions.question: What theological conclusion is drawn from that evidence?
questions.answer: It leads to the conclusion that Prophet Muhammad’s messengership is a necessary reality.

questions.question: What chain of ideas connects beauty in creation to messengership?
questions.answer: Beauty shows divine will to beautify, which shows love of perfection, which points to a highest conscious responder, which leads to the Messenger.

questions.question: Why is man described as the most enlightened and complete being in this argument?
questions.answer: Because man has the awareness to understand creation broadly and respond with conscious worship.

questions.question: What does the image of the tree and its fruit add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that the human being gathers and reflects the meanings of creation in a concentrated way.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the person among humanity who has the broadest vision?
questions.answer: That person should be the most exalted and radiant among human beings.

questions.question: What should such a person devote himself to?
questions.answer: He should devote himself fully to worshipping the Maker, appreciating divine artistry, and thanking Allah for blessings.

questions.question: Why does the passage describe one sphere as related to lordship and art?
questions.answer: To show the divine side of reality where power, order, and beauty are displayed.

questions.question: Why does it describe another sphere as related to worship and reflection?
questions.answer: To show the human side that consciously answers those divine displays.

questions.question: In what way does the second sphere serve the first?
questions.answer: It serves by recognizing, praising, admiring, and giving thanks for what the first sphere displays.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the rank of the one leading the second sphere?
questions.answer: He holds the highest rank among human responders and is especially near to Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the Maker’s generosity?
questions.answer: It portrays Him as so generous and attentive that even fine human preferences are considered.

questions.question: What would conflict with that generosity, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It would conflict with it to think that the Maker would ignore the most devoted and beautiful servant.

questions.question: What signs of devotion are mentioned regarding that servant?
questions.answer: He is described as praising, admiring, thanking, and exalting Allah with overwhelming intensity.

questions.question: What two honors are said to follow necessarily from his devotion?
questions.answer: Divine speech to him and his appointment as Messenger.

questions.question: How strongly does the passage reject the idea that these honors would not be given?
questions.answer: It rejects that idea completely and says it cannot be accepted.

questions.question: What concise faith statements conclude the passage?
questions.answer: That the religion before Allah is Islam and that Muhammad, peace be upon him, is the Messenger of Allah.

questions.question: What does the verse at the start of the passage command believers to do if they love Allah?
questions.answer: It commands them to follow the Prophet so that Allah will love them.

questions.question: How does the rest of the passage support that opening message?
questions.answer: It explains why the Prophet, peace be upon him, is the supreme guide whose mission is rooted in the meaning of creation itself.

questions.question: What feature of the universe is presented as plainly observable?
questions.answer: The beauty of its design and artistry is presented as plainly observable.

questions.question: What does this observed beauty prove about the Creator’s action?
questions.answer: It proves that the Creator acts with intentional beauty and adornment.

questions.question: What does intentional adornment suggest about the Creator’s relation to perfection?
questions.answer: It suggests a lofty love for the perfections manifested in creation.

questions.question: Why must this divine love be especially related to the human being?
questions.answer: Because the human being is the most conscious and comprehensive creature in the created order.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the human being’s place in the universe using a natural image?
questions.answer: It describes the human being as the fruit of the tree of creation.

questions.question: What is special about the human being who stands above others in awareness?
questions.answer: He has the widest outlook and deepest universal consciousness.

questions.question: What should he do with that broad awareness?
questions.answer: He should use it completely for worship, gratitude, and appreciation of Allah’s art.

questions.question: What does the passage say appears before us as two great displays?
questions.answer: It says there appears a display of divine rule and artistry and a display of worshipful reflection and faith.

questions.question: Which display is said to work in the name of the other?
questions.answer: The display of worship and reflection works in the name of the display of divine artistry and rule.

questions.question: What does this reveal about the one who leads the worshipful display?
questions.answer: It reveals that he is intimately tied to Allah’s purposes in creation and is deeply accepted by Him.

questions.question: How is the Maker described in relation to the creatures He has fashioned?
questions.answer: He is described as generous and as loving the art shown in those creatures.

questions.question: What argument from divine care is used to support the Prophet’s messengership?
questions.answer: If the Creator takes account of even small human enjoyments, then He would certainly not leave the greatest worshipper without revelation and mission.

questions.question: How is the Prophet’s devotion pictured in the passage?
questions.answer: It is pictured as powerful praise and gratitude that resound throughout creation.

questions.question: What outcome does the passage say necessarily follows from such devotion?
questions.answer: Allah would speak to him, make him His Messenger, and want others to follow his noble way.

questions.question: What final lesson should a student take from the closing lines of the passage?
questions.answer: That the truth of Islam and the messengership of Muhammad, peace be upon him, are presented as the fitting conclusion of reflecting on creation.
